sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: Feathery bog-moss has slender, narrow-leaved shoots. In pools it grows as soft, flaccid, floating or submerged tufts; this is among the most aquatic British Sphagnum species. The illustration’s loose green growth emerging from water matches that habit.

sections.title: Identification
sections.text: It also occurs in terrestrial forms, so wet habitat alone does not identify it. Species confirmation may require examining leaf and stem characters under magnification.

sections.title: Use and safety
sections.text: It is a peat-forming moss, not a food plant. Avoid removing it from natural bog pools and other protected wetland habitats.
